column2: Software Development using AI
UG

This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agentic software development processes, focusing on agent environment configuration, requirements decomposition, spec-driven planning, iterative development loops, execution tracing, and automated quality assessment. Designed for senior undergraduate students with strong software development fundamentals, the course enables learners to configure agentic development environments, decompose informal requirements into executable specifications, orchestrate iterative agent-assisted coding workflows, diagnose context-drift and failure causes from execution traces, and evaluate the reliability and maintainability of agent-generated software deliverables. Instruction is delivered through lectures, tutorials, laboratory sessions, and a semester-long project.

Course Code: Configure an agentic development environment integrating Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, context engineering assets, and external tool interfaces, for a modular software development task, meeting the stated interface specification for every public tool endpoint.
column2: Decompose informal software requirements into executable specifications, task plans, and structured context documents for autonomous coding agents, for a supplied multi-tier software feature, covering every use case in the supplied requirements document.
column3: Implement iterative agentic development workflows that orchestrate coding agents, tool interactions, and automated feedback loops, for a multi-component software project, such that at least 80% of the provided acceptance test cases pass.
column4: Diagnose anomalies, regressions, and context-drift failures in agent-assisted coding sessions, from supplied execution traces and automated test outputs, identifying at least three distinct failure causes with supporting log evidence.
column5: Evaluate the reliability, maintainability, and test coverage of agent-generated software deliverables, using automated testing frameworks and code review metrics, justifying each acceptance or rejection decision against at least one stated quality standard.
